{{short description|Theorem that the slice genus of the (p, q) torus knot is (p-1)(q-1)/2}}
{{otheruses|Milnor conjecture (disambiguation)}}
In [[knot theory]], the '''Milnor conjecture''' says that the [[slice genus]] of the <math>(p, q)</math> [[torus knot]] is

:<math>\frac{(p-1)(q-1)}{2}.</math>

It is in a similar vein to the [[Thom conjecture]].

The conjecture (named after [[John Milnor]]) was first proved by [[Gauge theory|gauge theoretic]] methods by [[Peter B. Kronheimer|Peter Kronheimer]] and [[Tomasz Mrowka]].<ref>{{citation|title=Gauge theory for embedded surfaces, I|first1=Peter B.|last1=Kronheimer|author-link1=Peter B. Kronheimer|first2=Tomasz S.|last2=Mrowka|author-link2=Tomasz Mrowka| journal=[[Topology (journal)|Topology]]|volume=32|issue=4|year=1993| pages=773–826|doi=10.1016/0040-9383(93)90051-V|doi-access=free|url=http://www.math.harvard.edu/~kronheim/thom1.pdf}}.</ref> Jacob Rasmussen later gave a purely [[combinatorial proof]] using [[Khovanov homology]], by means of the [[s-invariant]].<ref>{{Cite journal |last=Rasmussen |first=Jacob A.|year=2010 |title=Khovanov homology and the slice genus |url=http://link.springer.com/10.1007/s00222-010-0275-6 |journal=[[Inventiones Mathematicae]] |language=en |volume=182 |issue=2 |pages=419–447 |doi=10.1007/s00222-010-0275-6 |eprint=math.GT/0402131}}</ref>
